extracted.intended_audience: biotech/pharma product developers, academic groups, and other potential BARDA partners/applicants seeking funding or collaboration on medical countermeasures for influenza and emerging infectious diseases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and investment priorities from BARDA's Influenza & Emerging Infectious Diseases Division describing the kinds of medical countermeasures, capabilities, timelines, and program principles BARDA funds and prioritizes under its BAA. Useful for prospective applicants planning proposals or partnerships with BARDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: IEID Division Goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and sustain a portfolio of flexible MCM products and capabilities to protect the Nation in the next pandemic emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Division invests in products and capabilities that ensure on-demand availability to mitigate the next influenza pandemic, emphasizing rapid development, manufacturability, repurposability/re-engineerability, and sustainable domestic production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutics Program — novel antivirals for outpatient treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds novel antivirals to treat people with seasonal or pandemic influenza in outpatient settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA is interested in antiviral therapeutics that can be used early in disease (outpatient) to reduce severity and transmission; see AOIs 9.1–9.3 in the BAA for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutics Program — immune modulators and host-directed therapeutics
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds immune modulators and other host-directed therapeutics to treat and improve clinical outcomes of acute lung injury (ALI)/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) caused by pandemic and seasonal influenza and other pathogens of pandemic potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program has special interest in candidates that improve clinical outcomes in severe respiratory disease caused by influenza or other pandemic-potential pathogens; see referenced AOIs for specific solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutics Program — long-acting antivirals for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds long-acting antivirals to provide pre-exposure prophylaxis options against pandemic and seasonal influenza when vaccines are not yet available and for people whose immune systems may not generate a sufficient response from available vaccines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to approaches that can offer durable protection in advance of vaccine availability or for immunocompromised populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutics Program — biomarkers to stratify ALI/ARDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Special interest in identifying reliable biomarkers to stratify ALI/ARDS severity and target broad-label therapeutic candidates in specific populations suffering from or at risk of developing ALI/ARDS due to influenza or other pathogens with pandemic potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biomarker-driven stratification that enables targeted therapeutic use and clearer trial endpoints is a program priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — 100-day vaccine development goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance vaccine capabilities that can quickly develop vaccines from time of new virus threat identification to release of first vaccine doses for evaluation (goal: 100 days from sequence availability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA prioritizes platform and process innovations that materially reduce time-to-first-doses; proposals should demonstrate timelines and platforms supporting the 100-day objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — 120-day manufacturing scale-up goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Swiftly ramp-up existing or establish new manufacturing facilities to produce enough doses to immunize the U.S. population (goal: 120 days from sequence availability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should address raw material supply chains, surge capacity, and processes enabling 120-day population-scale production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — next-generation pandemic influenza vaccines
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizing improved and more rapidly produced next-generation pandemic influenza vaccines that decrease pandemic response time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies that materially reduce development and production timelines or otherwise improve pandemic responsiveness are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — technologies that improve vaccine effectiveness and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizing technologies that improve vaccine effectiveness and access (including alternative routes of administration that may expedite storage, shipping, and delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA values innovations that increase real-world effectiveness and broaden reach — e.g., alternative delivery routes, thermostability, simplified logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — platforms that modernize vaccine production
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizing platforms that modernize vaccine production processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on proven fast platform technologies with clinical and manufacturing experience as foundations for rapid product development and at-scale production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccine Development Program — end-to-end solutions to expand manufacturing capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizing end-to-end solutions that expand vaccine manufacturing capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose solutions that address the entire product lifecycle and manufacturing ecosystem to enable surge production and sustained supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Vaccines & Adjuvants — shorten response timelines and increase accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds partnerships that shorten pandemic response timelines and increase vaccine accessibility to ensure preparedness for a future influenza pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investments should demonstrably reduce time-to-deploy and improve equitable access to vaccines during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Vaccines & Adjuvants — manage National Pre-pandemic Influenza Vaccine Stockpile (NPIVS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manages the NPIVS, which holds pre-pandemic bulk antigens from influenza viruses with pandemic potential and is integral to pandemic preparedness and response capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that support stockpile maintenance, formulation readiness, or rapid use of NPIVS materials align with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Vaccines & Adjuvants — expand domestic vaccine manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanding domestic manufacturing of pandemic influenza vaccines to deliver enough doses to vaccinate the U.S. population during a public health emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority for investments that build sustainable domestic surge manufacturing capacity and reduce reliance on external supply chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Vaccines & Adjuvants — library of pre-pandemic vaccines and adjuvants
rubrics_metrics.description: Investing in a library of candidate pre-pandemic vaccines and licensed or authorized adjuvants to rapidly formulate enough vaccine doses to immunize critical care workers and at-risk populations early during a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for pre-formulated candidates and compatible adjuvants that enable rapid formulation and deployment is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic Vaccines & Adjuvants — clinical evaluation of stockpiled vaccines/adjuvants
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinically evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of stockpiled vaccines and adjuvants against influenza viruses with pandemic potential to enhance vaccine response readiness and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include plans for clinical testing/bridging studies to demonstrate readiness and effectiveness of stockpiled materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza Diagnostics & Devices — accuracy, robustness, and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds advanced development of accurate, robust, and accessible influenza tests to inform early treatment decisions, patient management, and public health interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should show analytical and clinical performance, operational robustness, and pathways to broad access (e.g., cost, distribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza Diagnostics & Devices — facilitate test-to-treat scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on tests that facilitate test-to-treat scenarios (e.g., provide accurate and rapid results to inform early consideration for antiviral drug use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic solutions that directly support early therapeutic decision-making and reduce time to treatment are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza Diagnostics & Devices — differentiate influenza A, B, and other respiratory viruses
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests should differentiate between Influenza A, Influenza B, and other respiratory viruses (like SARS-CoV-2 and RSV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplexing or differentiation capability to inform clinical and public health response is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza Diagnostics & Devices — detect novel influenza viruses
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable the detection of novel influenza viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostics with threat-agnostic or variant-detecting capabilities that can identify emerging/novel strains are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influenza Diagnostics & Devices — remove access barriers (pharmacy-use, at-home, low cost, automatic reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds innovative solutions that emphasize rapid pharmacy-use platforms, enable at-home testing, lower costs, and provide automatic result reporting for public health authorities to monitor viral circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Development plans should address usability in non-clinical settings, affordability, and integration with public health reporting systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BARDA Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) AOIs for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities for Influenza & EID are all under the BARDA Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), which supports advanced R&D of medical countermeasures; specific program investments reference AOIs (e.g., AOIs 7.3/7.4, 8.1/8.2, 9.1–9.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should consult the relevant AOIs in the BAA for details on scope, requirements, and submission instructions for each program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible Agreements (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexible partnerships with product developers allow BARDA to rapidly pivot to address new threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts and partnership structures that allow agility and rapid re-prioritization are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production Capacity (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring sufficient production capacity by leveraging platforms used for commercial product manufacturing — 'it does not matter how strong the safety and efficacy of a vaccine or therapeutic is if you cannot make enough of it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BARDA favors solutions that demonstrate scalable manufacturing and capacity to meet population-level needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform for Faster Development (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage proven fast platform technologies with extensive clinical trial and manufacturing experience as the foundation of rapid pandemic MCM product development and at-scale production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established platforms with prior clinical/manufacturing track records are considered lower risk and higher priority for rapid response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve Delivery (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seeking technologies that enable alternative ways to deliver vaccines — e.g., moving away from needle-and-syringe to adhesive patch self-application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery innovations that simplify administration, reduce need for specialized training, and ease logistics are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded Access (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in end-to-end solutions that prioritize diversity and inclusion, including clinical development plans that ensure that all populations will have access to these products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include plans ensuring equitable access across populations and inclusion in clinical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability (preparedness principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an updated portfolio of sustainable pandemic MCMs and capabilities, providing support when commercial markets are insufficient; conduct product life-cycle analyses as part of portfolio reviews to ensure continued availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals showing long-term supply sustainability, life-cycle planning, and strategies for maintaining availability outside of commercial incentives align with this principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy — prioritize flexible/repurposable products and domestic infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritizes products that can be developed and manufactured quickly, provide greater efficacy, and can be repurposed and/or re-engineered to allow for continuous at-scale production to supply the U.S. healthcare market; invests in flexible platform technologies and sustainable domestic MCM manufacturing infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that evidence repurposability, platform adaptability, and contribution to domestic manufacturing resilience are favored.
